title: Cycle-unit normalization of the explicit sheafification comparison
statement: Let C,R satisfy [def-per-local-rhom-normalization-interface] and fix QL0 isomorphic to K. For P,e,sigma of [lem-per-local-rhom-presheaf-model] and [lem-per-local-rhom-section-equivalence], let L,I be any complexes with I K-injective and k:QL to K an isomorphism. Use the augmentation-normalized representative comparison h of [lem-per-local-rhom-presheaf-model] and the concrete local map a of a sheaf cycle z from [lem-per-local-rhom-additive-cocycle-comparison]. Transport the cohomology class of z by h, source contravariance k inverse, and sigma inverse. The result equals the sheafification unit on the element corresponding under e to res(k inverse) followed by the localized a.

proof.text:
first take the source L₀ and a target equal to its fixed K-injective
resolution. The homology/sheafification comparison is induced by the maps on
cycles and their quotient. Its composite with the sheafification unit therefore
sends the section class of a cycle to its cohomology class. The kernel equation for the differential constructs sectionCycle directly,
and sectionCycle_i identifies it with the original component family. The canonical section comparison sends that class to the
localized sheafCycleMap. For a different K-injective target, the augmentation
is a quasi-isomorphism and its Hom map is a quasi-isomorphism; cancelling its
localized isomorphism gives kInjectiveRepresentativeIso. For a different source
representative, lift the comparison to chain maps into K-injective resolutions.
The component formula for the Hom bifunctor gives precomposition by k.inv;
localization naturality and the fixed coefficient factorization identify the
transported cohomology class. Applying these two transports to the first
equation gives the displayed formula for every representative.
